title: Gradient Boosting & the Tabular Frontier
subtitle: Fit the residuals, again and again: HistGradientBoosting, LightGBM, XGBoost, early stopping — and the tabular foundation models that, since 2025, beat tuned boosting on small data with zero tuning. Plus: the competition reveal

objectives.title: Explain Boosting in One Sentence
objectives.description: Start with a weak model, fit a small tree to its residuals, add it with a small learning rate, repeat. Bias falls step by step — and so, eventually, does generalization unless you stop early.

objectives.title: Drive the Three Big Libraries
objectives.description: scikit-learn's HistGradientBoosting with native categorical support, LightGBM, and XGBoost — same idea, different defaults. Learning rate, number of trees, depth, and regularization as the four knobs that matter.

objectives.title: Use Early Stopping Like a Professional
objectives.description: A validation set, a patience parameter, and the iteration where validation loss bottomed out. The single most important habit in boosting.

objectives.title: Place GBDTs on the 2026 Map
objectives.description: Tree ensembles beat neural networks on tabular data (Grinsztajn 2022). Tabular foundation models — TabPFN-2.5, TabICLv2 — now match or beat tuned boosting on small and medium tables. When to use which, and what licensing means for production.

bulletPoints: Public vs. private leaderboard shifts: the teams that overfit the public half fall; the teams that trusted cross-validation hold
Memos due on Canvas tonight at 11:59 PM

agenda.title: Boosting: Fit the Residuals
agenda.description: Bagging averages independent deep trees to cut variance. Boosting does the opposite: a sequence of shallow trees, each fit to what the ensemble so far got wrong, each added with a small learning rate. Bias falls with every tree. The picture: a regression curve improving one stump at a time.
bulletPoints: learning_rate × n_estimators: lower rate, more trees, smoother fit — 0.05 and 1,000 beats 0.5 and 100
Depth 3–8 trees, not depth-None: boosting wants weak learners

agenda.title: HistGradientBoosting, LightGBM, XGBoost
agenda.description: scikit-learn's HistGradientBoostingClassifier: histogram binning, native missing values, categorical_features='from_dtype'. LightGBM: the same idea, leaf-wise growth, blazing fast. XGBoost 3.x: the Kaggle veteran with the deepest regularization options. Same pipeline, three last steps.
bulletPoints: On hotel bookings all three land at AUC ≈ 0.95–0.96 out of the box — the differences are speed and knobs, not accuracy
CatBoost when categoricals dominate: ordered target statistics built in

agenda.title: Early Stopping & the Knobs That Matter
agenda.description: Plot training and validation log-loss against the number of trees. Training keeps falling; validation bottoms out and rises. early_stopping=True with a validation fraction and n_iter_no_change picks the bottom automatically. Then a quick tour of the regularizers: max_leaf_nodes, min_samples_leaf, l2_regularization, subsample.
bulletPoints: Early stopping is the boosting equivalent of the Overfitting Explorer's sweet spot — found automatically
Tune learning rate and tree count first; everything else is second-order

agenda.title: The Tabular Frontier: GBDT vs. Foundation Models
agenda.description: 2022: Grinsztajn et al. show tree ensembles beat deep learning on tabular data. 2025: TabPFN-2.5 — a transformer pretrained on millions of synthetic tables — wins against default XGBoost on nearly every dataset under 10k rows, with zero tuning, in seconds. 2026: TabICLv2 from Inria does it open-source at up to 500k rows. We run TabICL on a 5,000-row slice and compare.
bulletPoints: TFMs win small/medium data with no tuning; GBDTs win on scale, latency, and licensing (TabPFN-3 weights are non-commercial)
TabArena is the living leaderboard — check it before you pick a model for the final project

agenda.description: The 2026 default for tabular business data: a clean pipeline, early-stopped gradient boosting, and a tabular foundation model as the sanity check. Next week we learn to trust it: tuning, SHAP, conformal intervals, fairness.
bulletPoints: HW4 (due Nov 23): hotel bookings with boosting + SHAP — assigned in full next week

codeBlock.code:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

url = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harslan/isom-835/master/public/data/hotel_bookings.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(url)
leaks = ['reservation_status', 'reservation_status_date', 'assigned_room_type']
X = df.drop(columns=['is_canceled'] + leaks)
for c in X.select_dtypes(object): X[c] = X[c].astype('category')   # native categorical support
y = df['is_canceled']
X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=835)

gbm = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(
    learning_rate=0.05, max_iter=2000, max_leaf_nodes=31,
    early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.15, n_iter_no_change=50,
    categorical_features='from_dtype', random_state=835)
gbm.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
print(f'trees kept: {gbm.n_iter_}   test AUC: {roc_auc_score(y_te, gbm.predict_proba(X_te)[:, 1]):.3f}')

# Optional (Colab): the open-source tabular foundation model, zero tuning, small slice

activities.discussionNote: Early stopping is doing the work the Overfitting Explorer made you do by hand. And the foundation-model cell is the 2026 twist: on 5,000 rows a pretrained transformer with zero hyperparameters will typically match the boosted model you just tuned — in seconds. On 95,000 rows the GBDT pulls ahead again and runs in production without a license question. The right answer is now 'both': GBDT as the workhorse, a TFM as the fast baseline and the sanity check.

takeaways.text: Boosting fits the residuals sequentially with shallow trees and a small learning rate; it reduces bias where bagging reduces variance. Lower rate + more trees + early stopping is the recipe.
Early stopping on a validation set is the one habit that separates a boosting model that generalizes from one that memorized — and every major library has it built in.

On tabular business data tree ensembles still beat neural networks; since 2025 tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabICL) match tuned boosting on small and medium tables with zero tuning. Use a GBDT for scale, latency, and licensing; use a TFM as the instant baseline.
